claims.explanation: Aspirin's antiproliferative selectivity in this screen is most strongly associated with loss of wild-type p53 function, since nearly all selectively killed lines carry TP53 mutations while many unaffected lines retain wild-type TP53 or have mutations in other pathways. This is consistent with aspirin's known ability to activate AMPK and inhibit NF-kB/COX signaling, effects that are more cytotoxic in cells with defective p53-mediated stress responses. Additional sensitivity may be conferred by RAS/RTK-MAPK pathway activation (NRAS, BRAF, MAP2K1, EGFR) and by PTEN loss, which can amplify aspirin's AMPK-dependent growth suppression.

features.basis: Observed pattern: nearly all selectively killed lines carry TP53 mutations, while many unaffected lines have wild-type TP53 or non-TP53 drivers.
Observed pattern: NRAS-mutant melanoma and bladder lines are among the most killed; RAS-MAPK activation may cooperate with aspirin-induced AMPK stress.
Observed pattern: BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines appear in the sensitive set, suggesting MAPK-driven sensitivity.
Observed pattern: PTEN loss occurs in several highly sensitive lines (glioma, kidney, thyroid), possibly via enhanced PI3K-AKT dependence.
Observed pattern: NF1-mutant thyroid, glioma, and head/neck lines are among the most killed, consistent with RAS pathway activation.
Observed pattern: EGFR-mutant lung lines appear in the sensitive set, though some EGFR-mutant lines are also unaffected.
Observed pattern: one sensitive lung line carries MAP2K1 mutation, suggesting MAPK pathway activation.
Mechanism: aspirin inhibits COX-2 (PTGS2); high PTGS2 expression may reduce free drug or indicate dependence on prostaglandin signaling that aspirin only partially blocks.
Mechanism: aspirin acetylates COX-1 (PTGS1); high expression could buffer the antiplatelet/antiproliferative effect in some lines.
Mechanism: aspirin inhibits NF-kB signaling; elevated NF-kB may allow survival despite aspirin exposure.
Mechanism: aspirin activates AMPK; high AMPK catalytic subunit expression may enhance growth suppression.
Observed pattern: CDKN2A loss co-occurs in several sensitive lines, though it is also present in some resistant lines.
